title: Add optional effort estimates and effort sorting
lead:
Roadmap items have free-form `size` and priority axes, but no normalized estimate of
implementation weight. Add an optional `effort` field so people can compare and order
work by cost without changing what `next` considers important.
boundary:
**Not in this slice:** inferring effort from `size`; changing priority scores or `next`;
effort filters, statistics, or dependency-aware effort aggregation.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`size` is deliberately free text and cannot provide a reliable sort key. A small,
optional numeric effort axis makes implementation weight machine-readable while
allowing unestimated work to remain unset.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/model.py`, `ops.py`, `outline.py`, and `cli.py` — store, validate,
  mutate, import, expose, and sort effort
- `src/slicer/tui.py` and `tui_wizard.py` — edit and create the field interactively
- `src/slicer/render.py` and bundled templates — show effort in generated roadmaps
- CLI/model/import/TUI/render tests and user/agent documentation

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Old item JSON without `effort` loads with `effort=None`; new JSON and command JSON
   expose `fields.effort` as an integer or `null`.
2. `add --effort`, `set --effort`, outline `effort:`, the TUI editor, and the wizard
   accept only `1`, `2`, or `3`; omission leaves it unset and `set --no-effort` clears it.
3. Text and generated Markdown/HTML roadmap rows display `1`–`3` or `-` when unset.
4. `list --sort effort` orders assigned effort from `1` to `3`, puts unset items last,
   and preserves stored queue order for ties without writing state.
5. `sort --by effort` persists exactly that ordering and reports its normal moved count.
6. Default `list`, `next`, score sorting, dependency priority propagation, and existing
   projects remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Add `Item.effort: int | None = None` and serialize it in the fixed-order `fields` object.
Treat a missing key as `None` for backward compatibility. Share one validator for the
`1`–`3` range across add, set, import, and TUI paths. Add `--effort` to `add` and `set`,
`--no-effort` to `set`, and `effort:` to outline import and the import skeleton. Include
the field in TUI editing and roadmap creation.

Expose effort in text rows, JSON responses, generated Markdown, and generated HTML;
extend bundled templates without requiring existing custom templates to adopt the new
placeholder. Add `effort` to the accepted keys for read-only `list --sort` and mutating
`sort --by`. Use a shared stable key: assigned values ascending, then unset values,
with current queue order breaking ties. Keep the default sort mode and all priority
calculations unchanged. Document the field, clearing syntax, and ordering.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
An item can carry, clear, import, edit, display, and round-trip an optional effort from
1 to 3. Both view-only and persistent effort sorts put the lightest estimated work
first and unestimated work last, while normal prioritization behaves exactly as before.
